en.title: The MOBA Conundrum: Why We Still Can't Name Them After 10 Years
en.summary: A decade ago, gaming journalists tried to rebrand MOBAs with terms like 'wizard-'em-up.' Despite their valiant efforts, the awkward acronym persists, leaving many wondering if a better name is even possible.
en.body:
In the ever-shifting landscape of video game genres, some terms stick, while others, no matter how well-intentioned, fade into obscurity. For over a decade, the gaming press has wrestled with the nomenclature for a genre that dominates esports and boasts millions of dedicated players: the Multiplayer Online Battle Arena, or MOBA.

Back in 2014, former PC Gamer editor Chris Thursten famously threw his hat into the ring with a column titled "Why I am deadly serious about the phrase 'wizard-'em-up.'" This wasn't just a whimsical suggestion; it was a genuine attempt to find a more evocative and accurate descriptor for games that had evolved far beyond their Real-Time Strategy roots. The goal was to move past the clunky "MOBA," a term that, as many argue, describes every game and no game simultaneously. Another attempt, "lane-pushing game," fared no better, quickly becoming another footnote in the genre's naming saga.

## The Unwieldy Acronym's Reign

The reality is that **Dota 2** and **League of Legends** continue to thrive, their massive player bases and robust esports scenes a testament to the genre's enduring appeal. These games offer unparalleled strategic depth and the thrill of coordinated team play, constantly evolving with new content and balancing updates. While some titles, like **Heroes of the Storm**, experimented with removing traditional item systems and farming to focus more on "hero brawler" mechanics and team synchronization, the core appeal of competitive, objective-based team combat remains. The debate over what to call these games often feels secondary to the experience they provide: intense PvP showdowns where teamwork and split-second decisions are paramount.

## Why Does the Name Even Matter?

For fans, the genre's label might seem less critical than the hours spent mastering heroes, coordinating ganks, and pushing for victory. Yet, the struggle for a fitting name reflects a deeper conversation about how we categorize and understand complex game design. It highlights the difficulty of pinning down a genre that blends elements of action RPGs, RTS, and pure competitive multiplayer. As new games emerge and existing ones evolve, the MOBA tag, despite its flaws, has become a surprisingly persistent placeholder. It’s a testament to the genre's impact and the ongoing challenge of finding the *perfect* words to describe our favorite digital pastimes.

## What's Next

While a universally accepted new name for the MOBA genre remains elusive, its major players like **Dota 2** and **League of Legends** show no signs of slowing down. Expect continued updates, expansions, and esports events that will undoubtedly keep players engaged and fuel further discussion about what defines this dynamic genre.

content_raw: One of media's god-given powers is to coin phrases, one of our last remaining superpowers. Inspired by this post from Kieron Gillen, I wanted to take a moment to recall our noble-but-failed attempt to rename MOBAs (a miserable term that describes every game and no game) more than a decade ago. I am so out the loop that I have just learned folks use the phrase "imsim" now, and I'm tempted to come back to Games Journalism solely to kick everyone's asses. — @kierongillen.bsky.social ( @kierongillen.bsky.social.bsky.social ) 2026-09-21T21:09:28.760Z Just as Superman made the ultimate sacrifice against Doomsday, former PC Gamer editor Chris Thursten gave his editorial life to fix this awkwardly-named genre in his 2014 column, " Why I am deadly serious about the phrase 'wizard-'em-up .'" We also tried "lane-pushing game" for a span, yikes. The media business requires one to place bets.
